acceptance.given: A matrix aggregate is evaluated from evidence records whose matrix-case labels are intentionally incorrect while all other evidence fields remain parseable.

oracle.expected: The aggregate evaluation emits an invalid verdict and identifies mislabeled matrix evidence as the decisive reason.
forbidden: The aggregate is accepted or marked valid when matrix evidence labels are incorrect.
The verdict omits the label-mismatch cause.
oracle.observable: A validator result artifact records aggregate_status=invalid and a machine-readable matrix-label error for the mismatched evidence.

acceptance.then: Run the aggregate validator against the mislabeled matrix fixture and inspect the persisted verdict artifact.
acceptance.when: Matrix evidence is mislabeled during aggregate evaluation.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the aggregate-evaluation test with matrix-case labels altered so the implementation incorrectly accepts the aggregate.

slice_hint.behavior_change: The Toolchain aggregate evaluator must invalidate the aggregate whenever matrix evidence labels do not match their declared Matrix Cases, and must preserve the label-mismatch reason in its verdict evidence.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep existing aggregate verdict schema and reject only mislabeled matrix evidence; no state migration is required.

slice_hint.state_transition: mislabeled matrix evidence -> aggregate invalid verdict with explicit label-mismatch evidence
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The validator returns an invalid aggregate verdict and the verdict artifact contains the offending Matrix Case label mismatch.

acceptance.given: A replay produces a successful Replay Result containing target, capability, dependency, command, Probe, output, Consumer, snapshot, and non-authority binding facts.

oracle.expected: The successful Replay Result contains a distinct, independently evaluated Validator Capability verification record.
forbidden: Capability is inferred only from another replay field or from a different obligation's result.
The successful result omits the capability verification record.
oracle.observable: The replay result JSON includes a capability verification assertion with its own evidence reference and pass status.

acceptance.then: Inspect the successful Replay Result and verify the capability assertion is evaluated independently from the other replay facts.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the successful replay-result validation path with the Validator Capability assertion removed or derived solely from another assertion.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Successful replay validation must evaluate Validator Capability as a separate assertion and include its own evidence reference in the Replay Result.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Retain the existing Replay Result shape; add or preserve an independent capability assertion without changing unrelated verdict semantics.

slice_hint.state_transition: successful replay -> independent Validator Capability assertion recorded in Replay Result
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A successful Replay Result has a dedicated capability assertion whose evidence reference and pass/fail evaluation are independent of other assertions.

acceptance.given: The validator receives the complete Atomic Obligation set and witness relation for the current package.

oracle.expected: Validation reports exact reciprocal coverage for every Atomic Obligation and its corresponding witnesses, with no unmatched obligations or witnesses.
forbidden: Any Atomic Obligation lacks a witness link.
A witness relation is accepted when it is one-directional.
An unmatched witness is included in the relation.
oracle.observable: The exact-cover report contains equal obligation-to-witness and witness-to-obligation mappings and reports zero orphan nodes.

acceptance.then: Run the Exact Cover validator and inspect its reciprocal mapping and orphan-node counts.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the exact-cover validation case containing a missing reciprocal witness edge or an unmatched witness node.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Exact Cover validation must enforce both obligation-to-witness and witness-to-obligation mappings and reject any orphan obligation or witness node.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing coverage report format while adding reciprocal and orphan checks; no persisted-state migration.

slice_hint.state_transition: coverage relation supplied -> reciprocal exact-cover report or deterministic rejection
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The validator reports complete reciprocal mappings for every obligation and witness and zero orphan nodes; otherwise it fails.

acceptance.given: Validator source and execution are available, and validator content is evaluated as a separate subject from validator source and dependency closure.

oracle.expected: A verification record specifically evaluates validator content and records its own result and evidence.
forbidden: Validator content is treated as verified solely because validator source, capability, or another aspect was verified.
The record has no content-specific evidence.
oracle.observable: The verification artifact contains a validator-content assertion with an independent selector, command observation, and pass/fail result.

acceptance.then: Execute the validator-content check independently and inspect its content-specific verification record.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the validator verification path where content is marked verified without executing or recording a content-specific check.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Validator verification must execute a content-specific check and persist an independent result, rather than inheriting status from source or dependency checks.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep validator invocation and result schema compatible; add only the independent content assertion and evidence fields required by FR-3.

slice_hint.state_transition: validator content selected -> independent content verification record -> content verdict
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The validator emits a content-specific verification record with its own execution evidence and a deterministic result.
